summary: A framework that combines hierarchical prompts and disease-specific prototypes to classify brain disorders at multiple diagnostic levels. Evaluated on 54,360 subjects across six multi-center datasets, this work studies how structured diagnostic knowledge can guide image representation learning.
title: A hierarchical prompt and prototype learning framework for brain disorder classification

summary: A framework for predicting amyloid-β deposition from functional MRI, combining representations from a pretrained language model with task-oriented brain network learning. The study connects functional connectivity with a pathology-related target in Alzheimer’s disease research.
title: Amyloid-β Deposition Prediction With Large Language Model Driven and Task-Oriented Learning of Brain Functional Networks

summary: An adaptive graph meta-learner that transfers connectivity-based models to new brain disorder tasks with limited training data. Evaluation on 4,114 fMRI samples examines how shared connectivity representations can support adaptation across disease datasets.
title: Development and Fast Transferring of General Connectivity-Based Diagnosis Model to New Brain Disorders with Adaptive Graph Meta-Learner

summary: Joint learning of disease-related low- and high-order functional connectivity networks from resting-state fMRI. Graph attention captures interactions beyond pairs of brain regions, supporting the identification of mild cognitive impairment.
title: Learning Hierarchical-Order Functional Connectivity Networks for Mild Cognitive Impairment Diagnosis
DoctorGLM: Fine-tuning your Chinese Doctor is not a Herculean Task
summary: An open-source effort to adapt ChatGLM-6B to Chinese medical dialogue. I contributed to model training in this early exploration of accessible, healthcare-focused language models.
